issues.legal_issue: A party added after the filing deadline to a timely debt-adjustment proceeding continued under a successor statute is not added without jurisdiction when the court has power to add parties in that proceeding.
material_facts: An application for adjustment of a debt was filed within the time allowed under the earlier statute against a purchaser of the disputed lands.
The purchasers who later held the lands were added as parties after the earlier statute’s filing deadline; one was added before repeal and another after the successor statute came into force.
An appeal in the pending proceeding was continued under the successor statute, and the proceeding was thereafter dealt with under that statute.
issues.conclusion: The orders adding the appellants were not without jurisdiction, although an addition under the earlier statute might have been improper and liable to be set aside on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 7 and 17 of the Bombay Agricultural Debtors Relief Act, 1939, the Board could join necessary or proper parties, and an application had to be filed within the specified time. Section 56(2) of the Bombay Agricultural Debtors Relief Act, 1947 treated pending proceedings and appeals under the repealed Act as proceedings under the new Act, to be disposed of under its substantive and procedural provisions. Section 46 of the 1947 Act, including its proviso, empowered a court in a proper case to add or strike out parties under Order 1, rule 10, of the Code of Civil Procedure even after the specified filing dates. The Court relied on Vishwanath Mahadev Adhikari v. Krishnaji Ramchandra Bodas, A.I.R. 1949 Bom. 390; Hiraman Ratan v. Purshottam Deorao, A.I.R. 1953 Bom. 260; and Basavanappa Shivappa v. Neelappa Adiveppa, A.I.R. 1956 Bom. 201.

predicates.agricultural_debt_adjustment_proceeding: The matter was a proceeding seeking adjustment of an agricultural debtor’s debt.
predicates.timely_application_pending_at_transition: The debtor filed the adjustment application within the original filing period, and the proceeding remained pending when the replacement legal scheme took effect.
predicates.relevant_party_added_after_deadline: The court added a party connected to the property or claim after the original filing period had elapsed.

issues.definition: When a timely debt-adjustment proceeding remained pending through a change in the governing scheme and a relevant party was added after the filing deadline, the addition was not necessarily beyond the court’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A possessor does not acquire title by adverse possession when the period of possession is shorter than the required limitation period and an earlier period said to be capable of tacking is not proved.
material_facts: The appellants had possession of the disputed lands from 1934 until the debt-adjustment application was filed in 1945, a period shorter than twelve years.
The appellants contended that an earlier period should be added because the first respondent had occupied the lands as their tenant before they took possession.
The courts below found that the appellants had not proved that the first respondent occupied the lands as their tenant during that earlier period.
issues.conclusion: The appellants had not acquired title to the lands by adverse possession.
issues.legal_principle: The possession relied on for adverse possession had not continued for twelve years by the time the adjustment application was filed. The claimed earlier period could not be added because the alleged tenancy and possession during that period were not proved. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this issue in the judgment.

rule.if: agricultural_debt_adjustment_proceeding and adverse_possession_title_claim and possession_period_below_limitation and not prior_tacking_period_proven

predicates.agricultural_debt_adjustment_proceeding: The matter was a proceeding seeking adjustment of an agricultural debtor’s debt.
predicates.adverse_possession_title_claim: A party claimed ownership of the disputed property based on adverse possession.
predicates.possession_period_below_limitation: The party’s proved possession had not lasted for the full period required to acquire title by adverse possession.
predicates.prior_tacking_period_proven: The party proved an earlier period of possession that could be added to its own period of possession.

issues.definition: In a debt-adjustment proceeding, a claim to title by adverse possession fails when the proved possession is too short and the alleged earlier period to be added is not proved.
